item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q021_nad_binding_convergent_evolution","answer":"NAD(P) binding is not a single evolutionary label. In SCOPe 2.08, the classic NAD(P)-binding Rossmann-fold domains are fold c.2, SUNID 51734, in the alpha/beta class c, and their main homologous group is superfamily c.2.1, SUNID 51735. That superfamily contains multiple families, for example alcohol dehydrogenase-like C-terminal domains, tyrosine-dependent oxidoreductases, glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase-like N-terminal domains, formate/glycerate dehydrogenase NAD domains, and LDH N-terminal domain-like proteins. Those are reasonable divergent-evolution comparisons at the superfamily/family scale because SCOPe marks c.2.1 as a superfamily with homology implied by that level. SCOPe also has a distinct FAD/NAD(P)-binding-domain fold c.3, SUNID 51904, and superfamily c.3.1, SUNID 51905, with its own families such as adrenodoxin reductase-like C-terminal domains, FAD-linked reductases, succinate dehydrogenase/fumarate reductase flavoprotein N-terminal domains, and FAD/NAD-linked reductases. The presence of NAD(P)-using enzymes in both c.2/c.2.1 and c.3/c.3.1 therefore supports the point that the cofactor-binding problem has been solved in more than one structural lineage; a shared dinucleotide cofactor, a phosphate-binding loop, or a similar catalytic geometry by itself can be convergent rather than inherited from one common NAD(P)-binding ancestor. SCOPe class is still weaker evidence than fold or superfamily: both examples above are alpha/beta proteins, but that only says they mix helices and strands, not that their active sites or entire domains are homologous. A fold groups a whole-domain topology and is below class but above superfamily; it is not, by itself, a license to transfer detailed ancestry, enzyme specificity, exact domain boundaries, or template coordinates. A superfamily is the level at which SCOPe is asserting probable common ancestry, and a family is a still closer group within that superfamily. Thus NAD(P) binding and active-site resemblance should be used only as candidate evidence; homology and modeling templates require whole-domain sequence/structure support placing the compared domains in the same family or at least the same superfamily, and functions should not be transferred across different SCOPe folds or superfamilies solely because both bind NAD or NADP.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope.get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/current; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.2; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.2/parents","mcp__scope.get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/current; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.3; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.3/parents","mcp__scope.get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/current; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.2.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.2.1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51735; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51735/homology","mcp__scope.get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/current; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.3.1; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.3.1/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51905; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/51905/homology","mcp__scope.list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/current; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.2.1/children?limit=20","mcp__scope.list_scop_children: /api/v1/releases/current; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sccs/c.3.1/children?limit=50"]}]}
